new_entities.name: High serum PFAS burden
aliases: elevated serum per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances
new_entities.description: Above-background serum concentrations of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances measured in human biospecimens.

new_entities.name: Hepatic steatosis
new_entities.description: Excess hepatic fat accumulation, including nonalcoholic fatty liver disease or related steatosis phenotypes.

edges.effect_quant: Among 546 patients with acute coronary syndrome, each doubling in PFOS was associated with a 1.82% higher hepatic steatosis index and a 42% higher odds of MAFLD. In a larger NHANES-based analysis of 6,990 adults, PFAS mixtures showed positive, nearly linear associations with NAFLD risk score and liver function abnormalities, with triglycerides mediating part of the relationship.
edges.population: adults with measured serum PFAS concentrations, including acute coronary syndrome cohorts and general-population NHANES participants
edges.mechanism: PFAS may promote hepatic steatosis through lipid-handling disruption, triglyceride accumulation, and altered metabolic signaling in the liver. The human pattern still looks more associative than definitive, but it aligns with a mechanistic story centered on dysregulated lipid homeostasis.
edges.summary: High serum PFAS burden is increasingly associated with hepatic steatosis and related fatty-liver phenotypes in adults. The signal is not yet as mature as the PFAS-lipid literature, but recent human studies are consistent enough to treat fatty liver as a credible downstream risk rather than a speculative one.
edges.caveats: Current human data rely heavily on observational designs and risk scores or indirect steatosis indices rather than biopsy-confirmed disease. This edge should be read as an emerging metabolic-liver concern, not as final proof that PFAS directly cause fatty liver in every exposed population.

evidence.citation: YangM et al 2023 Ecotoxicol Environ Saf
evidence.notes: Association of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances with hepatic steatosis and metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease among patients with acute coronary syndrome.

effect_quant.comparator: each doubling in PFOS versus risk of MAFLD

evidence.citation: QiaoW et al 2025 Ecotoxicol Environ Saf
evidence.notes: Triglycerides mediate the relationships of per- and poly-fluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) exposure with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) risk in US participants.
